summary: Sonja Arntzen specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of British Columbia (~1968–1979) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz (~1974–1979) and was also taught by Seizan Yanagida (~1972–1974) and Sojo Hirano.

Sonja Glauch is a linguist who completed her Magisterexamen (~1987–1992), doctorate (~1992–1997), and Habilitation (~1997–2005) at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, where she also worked in 2007. Other posts included Heidelberg University Library, Vienna, and Munich.

Sonya S. Lee works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She completed a PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2004) under Hung Wu, Robert S. Nelson, and others. She held posts at Swarthmore, Stanford, and USC (attested 2010).

Soonil Hwang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at Dongguk University under Seung-won Seo and a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich. He later served as an editorial board member at Dongguk University.

Soorakkulame Pemaratana works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the National University of Singapore under thesis supervisor Saranindranath Tagore and is attested as a Visiting Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies in 2026.

Sophus Bugge was a linguist who studied at the universities of Oslo (~1851–1857), Copenhagen (~1857–1858), and Berlin (~1858–1859, under Albrecht Weber). He held posts at Uppsala University and the University of Oslo, where he became professor in 1866.
Soshu Nishioka is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held the post of professor at Shitennoji University, attested in 2000 and 2015.

Soshuku Shibatani works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and earned an MA and doctorate at Koyasan University. His posts include researcher at Koyasan University, lecturer at Sonoda Women's University, and secretary general at Junrei Henro Kenkyukai.

Sotan Oka was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He was a professor, dean, and president at Komazawa University, and founded Antai-ji in 1921.

Soyen Shaku was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Keio University and under teachers including Ekkei Shuken and Kōsen Imakita. He served as Zen master at Engaku-ji (1892) and president of Hanazono University (1914–1917).

Sravana Borkataky-Varma works in religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Delhi and completed a PhD at Rice University (~2010–2016), later teaching at Rice, Montana, UNC Wilmington, Harvard, and the University of Houston.

Sravani Kanamarlapudi specializes in linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Washington (2019) under Richard G. Salomon and is a PhD student at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indologist and historian. He studied at Visva-Bharati University, Andhra University, and the University of Marburg (~1963–1966, PhD). He served as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University (~1967–1997).
Sri Anirvan was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He completed his studies at the University of Calcutta, Sanskrit College and University, and the University of Dhaka.

Srikanth Kaul was an Indologist and historian. Attested in 1967, he held posts at Government Degree College, Sopore, and as a professor in the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir.

Srinivas H. Ritti was an Indologist and historian. He served as an Epigraphical Assistant for the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1964) and Government Epigraphist for India (attested 1965), and as a professor at Karnatak University (attested 1975).

Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Hamburg (~1960–1967). He subsequently served on the faculty at the University of Hamburg as Privatdozent für Indologie from 1973 to 1997.

Sriram Krishnan specializes in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics. He has held posts at Central Sanskrit University, the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad, and the University of Hyderabad.

Srisa Chandra Vasu was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Government College University, Lahore. He founded the Panini Office in 1891, served as a vakil at the Allahabad High Court, and was a fellow at the University of Allahabad.

Stacey Van Vleet specializes in Tibetology, history/archaeology, and Sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Colorado Boulder, studied under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, and received a PhD and held an appointment at Columbia University.
